status: Stable planning-key ownership simplified; full acceptance remains open
implementation: A shared internStableDataKey helper reserves formatting output before construction, reuses an existing immutable key when equal, and transfers the reservation directly for a new key.
Window planning no longer creates a child scope and multiple retained handles for each key. Stable serialization forecasting and equal-string backing reuse are preserved.
Reservation ownership remains with the caller on transfer-validation failure and is released by the helper; successful transfer leaves the key owned by the supplied scope.

default.note: Full run before adding the final stage-transfer regression; production sources unchanged afterward.

focusedFinal.scope: Checkpoint encoding and window-planning tests, including three new regressions for equal-key reuse, exact peak/minus-one boundaries, and stage transfer without a second budget reservation.

validation.build: pnpm exec tsc -b passed before runtime tests and benchmarks
validation.limitations: Coverage, external conformance and full packaging were not refreshed for this change.

performance.tradeoff: Compatible plans still cost more with admission than the untracked baseline (2.437109 ms in the current report). No memory checks were removed to obtain the improvement.
performance.method: Same local benchmark with two warmups, three samples, independent group membership/order assertions and final zero-reservation checks. Reports retain raw samples; timing variation remains relevant.
performance.limitations: Planning kernels only; no cloud latency or total VM heap claim.

remainingAcceptance: Low-headroom alternatives for cached planning, remaining planning/metadata and timestamp workspace admission remain open.
Legacy spill-read pre-allocation admission, delegated task intermediates, transactional spill cleanup and other source/operator gaps remain open.
Full mixed-job/adaptive scheduling acceptance and production Cloudflare total-memory evidence remain open.
Reservation accounting does not establish total VM heap, external backing or RSS limits.
